sanskrit: vṛtrād bhītais tadā devair balam indre samarpitam tāny ekasthāni sarvāṇi tatas tvaṃ pratipatsyase
english: The gods, frightened of Vṛtra, then entrusted all their power to Indra; all of that collected in one place — you shall then obtain it all.

sanskrit: śakram eva prapadyasva sa te 'strāṇi pradāsyati dīkṣito 'dyaiva gaccha tvaṃ draṣṭuṃ devaṃ puraṃdaram
english: Seek refuge with Śakra alone; he will bestow the weapons upon you. Be consecrated this very day and go to behold the god who shatters citadels, Purandara.

sanskrit: evam uktvā dharmarājas tam adhyāpayata prabhuḥ dīkṣitaṃ vidhinā tena yatavākkāyamānasam anujajñe tato vīraṃ bhrātā bhrātaram agrajaḥ
english: Having spoken thus, the lord Dharmarāja himself instructed him; the elder brother then gave leave to that hero, his brother, duly consecrated, with speech, body and mind fully restrained.

sanskrit: nideśād dharmarājasya draṣṭuṃ devaṃ puraṃdaram dhanur gāṇḍīvam ādāya tathākṣayyau maheṣudhī
english: By the command of Dharmarāja, to behold the god Purandara, he took up the bow Gāṇḍīva and likewise the two inexhaustible great quivers.

sanskrit: kavacī satalatrāṇo baddhagodhāṅgulitravān hutvāgniṃ brāhmaṇān niṣkaiḥ svasti vācya mahābhujaḥ
english: Clad in armour, with arm-guard and finger-guard fastened on, the mighty-armed one offered oblations to the fire, honoured the brahmins with golden gifts, and had auspicious verses recited.

sanskrit: prātiṣṭhata mahābāhuḥ pragṛhītaśarāsanaḥ vadhāya dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ niḥśvasyordhvam udīkṣya ca
english: The mighty-armed one set forth, bow in hand, to slay the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, breathing deeply and gazing upward.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā tatra kaunteyaṃ pragṛhītaśarāsanam abruvan brāhmaṇāḥ siddhā bhūtāny antarhitāni ca kṣipraṃ prāpnuhi kaunteya manasā yad yad icchasi
english: Seeing that son of Kuntī there with bow raised, brahmins, siddhas, and invisible beings all spoke: "Swiftly attain, O son of Kuntī, whatever your mind desires."

sanskrit: taṃ siṃham iva gacchantaṃ śālaskandhorum arjunam manāṃsy ādāya sarveṣāṃ kṛṣṇā vacanam abravīt
english: As Arjuna moved away like a lion, his thighs like the trunk of a śāla tree, Kṛṣṇā, having captured the minds of all, spoke these words.

sanskrit: yat te kuntī mahābāho jātasyaicchad dhanaṃjaya tat te 'stu sarvaṃ kaunteya yathā ca svayam icchasi
english: "Whatever Kuntī desired for you when you were born, O mighty-armed Dhanañjaya — may all of that be yours, O son of Kuntī, and even more as you yourself may wish."

sanskrit: māsmākaṃ kṣatriyakule janma kaś cid avāpnuyāt brāhmaṇebhyo namo nityaṃ yeṣāṃ yuddhe na jīvikā
english: "Let no one be born into our kṣatriya family — everlasting homage to the brahmins, whose livelihood does not depend on battle."

sanskrit: nūnaṃ te bhrātaraḥ sarve tvatkathābhiḥ prajāgare raṃsyante vīrakarmāṇi kīrtayantaḥ punaḥ punaḥ
english: "Surely all your brothers, keeping vigil, will delight in tales of you, praising your heroic deeds again and again."

sanskrit: naiva naḥ pārtha bhogeṣu na dhane nota jīvite tuṣṭir buddhir bhavitrī vā tvayi dīrghapravāsini
english: "O Pārtha, neither in pleasures nor in wealth nor in life itself will our satisfaction or our thoughts exist while you are long away."

sanskrit: tvayi naḥ pārtha sarveṣāṃ sukhaduḥkhe samāhite jīvitaṃ maraṇaṃ caiva rājyam aiśvaryam eva ca āpṛṣṭo me 'si kaunteya svasti prāpnuhi pāṇḍava
english: "In you, O Pārtha, all our happiness and sorrow are concentrated — life and death itself, kingdom and lordship alike. You have taken leave of me, O son of Kuntī; go well, O Pāṇḍava."

sanskrit: namo dhātre vidhātre ca svasti gaccha hy anāmayam svasti te 'stv āntarikṣebhyaḥ pārthivebhyaś ca bhārata divyebhyaś caiva bhūtebhyo ye cānye paripanthinaḥ
english: "Homage to Dhātṛ and Vidhātṛ! Go well and unharmed. May you be protected from aerial beings, O Bhārata, from earthly ones, from divine beings, and from whatever other adversaries there may be."

sanskrit: tataḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā bhrātṝn dhaumyaṃ ca pāṇḍavaḥ prātiṣṭhata mahābāhuḥ pragṛhya ruciraṃ dhanuḥ
english: Then, having circumambulated his brothers and Dhaumya, the mighty-armed Pāṇḍava set forth, taking up his splendid bow.

sanskrit: tasya mārgād apākrāman sarvabhūtāni gacchataḥ yuktasyaindreṇa yogena parākrāntasya śuṣmiṇaḥ
english: All beings drew aside from his path as he went, for he was endowed with Indra's divine power and was mighty with valor and energy.

sanskrit: so 'gacchat parvataṃ puṇyam ekāhnaiva mahāmanāḥ manojavagatir bhūtvā yogayukto yathānilaḥ
english: He, the great-souled one, reached the sacred mountain in a single day, moving with the speed of thought, united in yoga like the wind itself.

sanskrit: himavantam atikramya gandhamādanam eva ca atyakrāmat sa durgāṇi divārātram atandritaḥ
english: Crossing the Himālaya and Gandhamādana as well, he traversed those difficult mountain passes day and night without fatigue.

sanskrit: indrakīlaṃ samāsādya tato 'tiṣṭhad dhanaṃjayaḥ antarikṣe hi śuśrāva tiṣṭheti sa vacas tadā
english: Reaching Indrakīla, Dhanañjaya then halted, for he heard a voice in the sky saying: "Stay here."

sanskrit: tato 'paśyat savyasācī vṛkṣamūle tapasvinam brāhmyā śriyā dīpyamānaṃ piṅgalaṃ jaṭilaṃ kṛśam
english: Then the left-handed archer saw at the foot of a tree an ascetic blazing with brahminical splendour — tawny-coloured, matted-haired and lean.

sanskrit: so 'bravīd arjunaṃ tatra sthitaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahātapāḥ kas tvaṃ tāteha saṃprāpto dhanuṣmān kavacī śarī nibaddhāsitalatrāṇaḥ kṣatradharmam anuvrataḥ
english: That great ascetic, seeing Arjuna standing there, said: "Who are you, dear one, who has arrived here bearing a bow, clad in armour, with arrows, arm-guard fastened on, following the dharma of a kṣatriya?"

sanskrit: neha śastreṇa kartavyaṃ śāntānām ayam ālayaḥ vinītakrodhaharṣāṇāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ tapasvinām
english: "Here there is no use for weapons; this is the abode of the peaceful, of brahmins and ascetics who have subdued anger and joy."

sanskrit: nehāsti dhanuṣā kāryaṃ na saṃgrāmeṇa karhi cit nikṣipaitad dhanus tāta prāpto 'si paramāṃ gatim
english: "There is no purpose here for a bow, nor for battle at any time. Set down this bow, dear one — you have reached the highest path."

sanskrit: ity anantaujasaṃ vīraṃ yathā cānyaṃ pṛthagjanam tathā vācam athābhīkṣṇaṃ brāhmaṇo 'rjunam abravīt na cainaṃ cālayām āsa dhairyāt sudṛḍhaniścayam
english: Thus the brahmin kept addressing that hero of boundless might repeatedly, just as he would address an ordinary man, yet he could not shake him from his composure, firm and resolute in his determination.

sanskrit: tam uvāca tataḥ prītaḥ sa dvijaḥ prahasann iva varaṃ vṛṇīṣva bhadraṃ te śakro 'ham arisūdana
english: Then that twice-born one, pleased and as if smiling, said to him: "Choose a boon — good fortune to you! I am Śakra, O destroyer of enemies."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ pratyuvāca sahasrākṣaṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ prāñjaliḥ praṇato bhūtvā śūraḥ kurukulodvahaḥ
english: Thus addressed, Dhanañjaya, the hero and upholder of the Kuru lineage, bowed with joined palms and replied to the thousand-eyed one.

sanskrit: īpsito hy eṣa me kāmo varaṃ cainaṃ prayaccha me tvatto 'dya bhagavann astraṃ kṛtsnam icchāmi veditum
english: "This is indeed my cherished desire; grant me this boon: from you, O blessed one, I wish today to learn the whole science of weapons."

sanskrit: pratyuvāca mahendras taṃ prītātmā prahasann iva iha prāptasya kiṃ kāryam astrais tava dhanaṃjaya kāmān vṛṇīṣva lokāṃś ca prāpto 'si paramāṃ gatim
english: The great Indra replied to him, his heart pleased and as if smiling: "What need of weapons do you have now that you have arrived here, O Dhanañjaya? Choose desires and worlds — you have reached the highest state."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ pratyuvāca sahasrākṣaṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ na lokān na punaḥ kāmān na devatvaṃ kutaḥ sukham
english: Thus addressed, Dhanañjaya replied to the thousand-eyed one: "Not worlds, nor desires once more, nor divinity — how much less pleasure!"

sanskrit: na ca sarvāmaraiśvaryaṃ kāmaye tridaśādhipa bhrātṝṃs tān vipine tyaktvā vairam apratiyātya ca akīrtiṃ sarvalokeṣu gaccheyaṃ śāśvatīḥ samāḥ
english: "Nor do I desire sovereignty over all the immortals, O lord of the thirty gods — for leaving those brothers of mine in the forest and failing to requite the enmity, I would bear infamy in all the worlds for eternal ages."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ pratyuvāca vṛtrahā pāṇḍunandanam sāntvayañ ślakṣṇayā vācā sarvalokanamaskṛtaḥ
english: Thus addressed, the slayer of Vṛtra, worshipped by all the worlds, replied to the son of Pāṇḍu, soothing him with gentle speech.

sanskrit: yadā drakṣyasi bhūteśaṃ tryakṣaṃ śūladharaṃ śivam tadā dātāsmi te tāta divyāny astrāṇi sarvaśaḥ
english: "When you behold the lord of all beings, the three-eyed Śiva who bears the trident, then, dear one, I shall grant you all the divine weapons completely."

sanskrit: kriyatāṃ darśane yatno devasya parameṣṭhinaḥ darśanāt tasya kaunteya saṃsiddhaḥ svargam eṣyasi
english: "Make effort to obtain a vision of the highest god; by the sight of him, O son of Kuntī, you will be perfected and will attain heaven."

sanskrit: ity uktvā phalgunaṃ śakro jagāmādarśanaṃ tataḥ arjuno 'py atha tatraiva tasthau yogasamanvitaḥ
english: Having spoken thus to Phalguna, Śakra then vanished from sight. And Arjuna too remained right there, absorbed in yoga.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca bhagavañ śrotum icchāmi pārthasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ vistareṇa kathām etāṃ yathāstrāṇy upalabdhavān
english: Janamejaya said: "O blessed one, I wish to hear at length this account of Pārtha of tireless deeds — how he obtained the weapons."

sanskrit: kathaṃ sa puruṣavyāghro dīrghabāhur dhanaṃjayaḥ vanaṃ praviṣṭas tejasvī nirmanuṣyam abhītavat
english: "How did that tiger among men, the long-armed radiant Dhanañjaya, enter the forest void of humans without fear?"

sanskrit: kiṃ ca tena kṛtaṃ tatra vasatā brahmavittama kathaṃ ca bhagavān sthāṇur devarājaś ca toṣitaḥ
english: "And what did he do while dwelling there, O best of knowers of Brahman? How were the blessed Sthāṇu and the king of the gods both pleased?"

sanskrit: etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ tvatprasādād dvijottama tvaṃ hi sarvajña divyaṃ ca mānuṣaṃ caiva vettha ha
english: "This I wish to hear through your grace, O best of twice-born ones, for you, the all-knowing, understand both divine and human matters."

sanskrit: atyadbhutaṃ mahāprājña romaharṣaṇam arjunaḥ bhavena saha saṃgrāmaṃ cakārāpratimaḥ kila purā praharatāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ saṃgrāmeṣv aparājitaḥ
english: "O greatly wise one, it is said that Arjuna, peerless in battle, the foremost of fighters and undefeated in combat, once fought an incomparable battle with Bhava — most wonderful and thrilling to hear."

sanskrit: yac chrutvā narasiṃhānāṃ dainyaharṣātivismayāt śūrāṇām api pārthānāṃ hṛdayāni cakampire
english: "Hearing of which, the hearts of even the heroic sons of Pṛthā trembled with a mingling of awe, elation and wonder."

sanskrit: yad yac ca kṛtavān anyat pārthas tad akhilaṃ vada na hy asya ninditaṃ jiṣṇoḥ susūkṣmam api lakṣaye caritaṃ tasya śūrasya tan me sarvaṃ prakīrtaya
english: "And whatever else Pārtha did — recount all of it in full. For I see not even the slightest reprehensible act in the deeds of that victorious hero. Tell me everything of that brave one's conduct."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca kathayiṣyāmi te tāta kathām etāṃ mahātmanaḥ divyāṃ kauravaśārdūla mahatīm adbhutopamām
english: Vaiśampāyana said: "I shall narrate to you, dear one, this account of the great-souled one — divine, great and of incomparable wonder, O tiger of the Kurus."

sanskrit: gātrasaṃsparśasaṃbandhaṃ tryambakeṇa sahānagha pārthasya devadevena śṛṇu samyak samāgamam
english: "Hear attentively, O sinless one, the bodily contact and encounter between Pārtha and the three-eyed god of gods, that meeting in its proper order."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraniyogāt sa jagāmāmitavikramaḥ śakraṃ sureśvaraṃ draṣṭuṃ devadevaṃ ca śaṃkaram
english: "By Yudhiṣṭhira's command that one of boundless valour went to behold Śakra, the lord of the gods, and also Śaṃkara, the god of gods."

sanskrit: divyaṃ tad dhanur ādāya khaḍgaṃ ca puruṣarṣabhaḥ mahābalo mahābāhur arjunaḥ kāryasiddhaye diśaṃ hy udīcīṃ kauravyo himavacchikharaṃ prati
english: "Taking up that divine bow and also his sword, Arjuna, that bull among men, mighty and great-armed, O Kauravya, set out toward the north, toward the peaks of the Himālaya, for the accomplishment of his purpose."

sanskrit: aindriḥ sthiramanā rājan sarvalokamahārathaḥ tvarayā parayā yuktas tapase dhṛtaniścayaḥ vanaṃ kaṇṭakitaṃ ghoram eka evānvapadyata
english: "The son of Indra, O king, steady of mind, the great warrior of all the worlds, filled with utmost urgency, firm in his resolve for austerity, entered alone into the terrible thorny forest."

sanskrit: nānāpuṣpaphalopetaṃ nānāpakṣiniṣevitam nānāmṛgagaṇākīrṇaṃ siddhacāraṇasevitam
english: "It was adorned with various flowers and fruits, frequented by various birds, filled with herds of various animals, and haunted by siddhas and cāraṇas."

sanskrit: tataḥ prayāte kaunteye vanaṃ mānuṣavarjitam śaṅkhānāṃ paṭahānāṃ ca śabdaḥ samabhavad divi
english: "Then, when the son of Kuntī had set forth into that forest devoid of humans, the sound of conches and kettledrums arose in the sky."

sanskrit: puṣpavarṣaṃ ca sumahan nipapāta mahītale meghajālaṃ ca vitataṃ chādayām āsa sarvataḥ
english: "And a great shower of flowers fell upon the earth, while a vast web of clouds spread over and covered everything on all sides."

sanskrit: atītya vanadurgāṇi saṃnikarṣe mahāgireḥ śuśubhe himavatpṛṣṭhe vasamāno 'rjunas tadā
english: "Having crossed the difficult forest passes, near the great mountain, Arjuna dwelling on the slopes of the Himālaya shone with beauty."

sanskrit: tatrāpaśyad drumān phullān vihagair valgu nāditān nadīś ca bahulāvartā nīlavaiḍūryasaṃnibhāḥ
english: "There he beheld trees in full bloom, sweetly ringing with birds, and rivers with many eddies resembling dark-blue lapis lazuli."

sanskrit: haṃsakāraṇḍavodgītāḥ sārasābhirutās tathā puṃskokilarutāś caiva krauñcabarhiṇanāditāḥ
english: "They resounded with the songs of geese and karaṇḍava ducks, the calls of sārasa cranes, the cries of male cuckoos, and the clamour of krauñca birds and peacocks."

sanskrit: manoharavanopetās tasminn atiratho 'rjunaḥ puṇyaśītāmalajalāḥ paśyan prītamanābhavat
english: "Seeing in that place the charming forested regions, and the sacred, cool, clear waters, Arjuna, that supreme chariot-warrior, became delighted in heart."

sanskrit: ramaṇīye vanoddeśe ramamāṇo 'rjunas tadā tapasy ugre vartamāna ugratejā mahāmanāḥ
english: "Arjuna, then delighting in that pleasant forest region, engaged in fierce austerity, blazing with fierce energy, great-souled."

sanskrit: darbhacīraṃ nivasyātha daṇḍājinavibhūṣitaḥ pūrṇe pūrṇe trirātre tu māsam ekaṃ phalāśanaḥ dviguṇenaiva kālena dvitīyaṃ māsam atyagāt
english: "Wearing a robe of darbha grass, adorned with staff and deer-skin, eating only fruit once every three full nights, he passed the first month; and with doubly extended intervals he passed the second month."

sanskrit: tṛtīyam api māsaṃ sa pakṣeṇāhāram ācaran śīrṇaṃ ca patitaṃ bhūmau parṇaṃ samupayuktavān
english: "In the third month too, he ate only once a fortnight, subsisting on withered leaves that had fallen to the ground."

sanskrit: caturthe tv atha saṃprāpte māsi pūrṇe tataḥ param vāyubhakṣo mahābāhur abhavat pāṇḍunandanaḥ ūrdhvabāhur nirālambaḥ pādāṅguṣṭhāgraviṣṭhitaḥ
english: "When the fourth full month arrived, thereafter the mighty-armed son of Pāṇḍu subsisted on air alone — arms raised high, unsupported, standing on the tips of his great toes."

sanskrit: sadopasparśanāc cāsya babhūvur amitaujasaḥ vidyudambhoruhanibhā jaṭās tasya mahātmanaḥ
english: "Through his constant contact with water, the matted locks of that great-souled one of boundless energy came to resemble lightning and the lotus clouds."

sanskrit: tato maharṣayaḥ sarve jagmur devaṃ pinākinam śitikaṇṭhaṃ mahābhāgaṃ praṇipatya prasādya ca sarve nivedayām āsuḥ karma tat phalgunasya ha
english: "Then all the great seers went to the divine bearer of the Pināka, the blue-throated one of great fortune, and prostrating themselves and propitiating him, they all reported that deed of Phalguna."

sanskrit: eṣa pārtho mahātejā himavatpṛṣṭham āśritaḥ ugre tapasi duṣpāre sthito dhūmāyayan diśaḥ
english: "This Pārtha of great energy has taken to the slopes of the Himālaya and stands fixed in fierce, unapproachable austerity, sending smoke into all the directions."

sanskrit: tasya deveśa na vayaṃ vidmaḥ sarve cikīrṣitam saṃtāpayati naḥ sarvān asau sādhu nivāryatām
english: "O lord of the gods, none of us know what he intends; he is causing us all distress — please, let him be properly restrained."

sanskrit: maheśvara uvāca śīghraṃ gacchata saṃhṛṣṭā yathāgatam atandritāḥ aham asya vijānāmi saṃkalpaṃ manasi sthitam
english: Maheśvara said: "Go back quickly, joyful and without fatigue, the same way you came. I know the resolve that abides in his mind."

sanskrit: nāsya svargaspṛhā kā cin naiśvaryasya na cāyuṣaḥ yat tv asya kāṅkṣitaṃ sarvaṃ tat kariṣye 'ham adya vai
english: "He has no longing for heaven, nor for lordship, nor for long life. Whatever is desired by him in full — that I shall accomplish this very day."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca te śrutva śarvavacanam ṛṣayaḥ satyavādinaḥ prahṛṣṭamanaso jagmur yathāsvaṃ punar āśramān
english: Vaiśampāyana said: "Hearing the words of Śarva, those seers who speak the truth returned, their hearts rejoiced, each to their own hermitage."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca gateṣu teṣu sarveṣu tapasviṣu mahātmasu pinākapāṇir bhagavān sarvapāpaharo haraḥ
english: Vaiśampāyana said: "When all those great-souled ascetics had departed, the blessed Hara who bears the Pināka and removes all sins —

sanskrit: kairātaṃ veṣam āsthāya kāñcanadrumasaṃnibham vibhrājamāno vapuṣā girir merur ivāparaḥ
english: — assuming the guise of a Kirāta hunter, resembling a golden tree, blazing with his form like another Mount Meru —

sanskrit: śrīmad dhanur upādāya śarāṃś cāśīviṣopamān niṣpapāta mahārciṣmān dahan kakṣam ivānalaḥ
english: — taking up a splendid bow and arrows like venomous serpents, descended with great blazing radiance, burning like fire consuming dry grass.

sanskrit: devyā sahomayā śrīmān samānavrataveṣayā nānāveṣadharair hṛṣṭair bhūtair anugatas tadā
english: Accompanied by the goddess Umā, dressed in matching vow and garb, and attended by joyful beings wearing various costumes, the glorious one came thus.

sanskrit: kirātaveṣapracchannaḥ strībhiś cānu sahasraśaḥ aśobhata tadā rājan sa devo 'tīva bhārata
english: Concealed in the guise of a Kirāta hunter, followed by thousands of women, that god then shone exceedingly, O king, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: kṣaṇena tad vanaṃ sarvaṃ niḥśabdam abhavat tadā nādaḥ prasravaṇānāṃ ca pakṣiṇāṃ cāpy upāramat
english: In an instant that entire forest became silent; the sound of streams ceased, and even the birds fell quiet.

sanskrit: sa saṃnikarṣam āgamya pārthasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ mūkaṃ nāma diteḥ putraṃ dadarśādbhutadarśanam
english: Approaching nearby, he saw a son of Diti named Mūka near the one of tireless deeds, Pārtha — a being of astonishing appearance.

sanskrit: vārāhaṃ rūpam āsthāya tarkayantam ivārjunam hantuṃ paramaduṣṭātmā tam uvācātha phalgunaḥ
english: Having assumed the form of a boar and seeming to stalk Arjuna for the kill, that supremely evil-souled one was then addressed by Phalguna.

sanskrit: gāṇḍīvaṃ dhanur ādāya śarāṃś cāśīviṣopamān sajyaṃ dhanurvaraṃ kṛtvā jyāghoṣeṇa ninādayan
english: Taking up the Gāṇḍīva bow and arrows like venomous serpents, stringing that best of bows and making it resound with the twang of its string —

sanskrit: yan māṃ prārthayase hantum anāgasam ihāgatam tasmāt tvāṃ pūrvam evāhaṃ neṣyāmi yamasādanam
english: "Because you seek to kill me, guiltless as I am who have come here — therefore I shall send you first to the abode of Yama."

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā prahariṣyantaṃ phalgunaṃ dṛḍhadhanvinam kirātarūpī sahasā vārayām āsa śaṃkaraḥ
english: Seeing Phalguna with bow firmly drawn, about to strike, Śaṃkara in the form of a Kirāta suddenly restrained him.

sanskrit: mayaiṣa prārthitaḥ pūrvaṃ nīlameghasamaprabhaḥ anādṛtyaiva tad vākyaṃ prajahārātha phalgunaḥ
english: "This one dark as a rain-cloud was claimed by me first" — but disregarding that very word, Phalguna then struck.

sanskrit: kirātaś ca samaṃ tasminn ekalakṣye mahādyutiḥ pramumocāśaniprakhyaṃ śaram agniśikhopamam
english: And the Kirāta of great radiance simultaneously into that same single target released an arrow like a thunderbolt, like a flame of fire.

sanskrit: tau muktau sāyakau tābhyāṃ samaṃ tatra nipetatuḥ mūkasya gātre vistīrṇe śailasaṃhanane tadā
english: Those two arrows released by both of them fell simultaneously on the vast, mountain-solid body of Mūka.

sanskrit: yathāśaniviniṣpeṣo vajrasyeva ca parvate tathā tayoḥ saṃnipātaḥ śarayor abhavat tadā
english: Like the crash of a thunderbolt, like Vajra striking a mountain, so was the collision of those two arrows then.

sanskrit: sa viddho bahubhir bāṇair dīptāsyaiḥ pannagair iva mamāra rākṣasaṃ rūpaṃ bhūyaḥ kṛtvā vibhīṣaṇam
english: Pierced by many arrows like blazing-mouthed serpents, he died, having once more assumed a terrible rākṣasa form.
